reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to turn any real number into a decision between zero and one. If we simply scale numbers, huge inputs break our bounds. We need a curve that flattens out at both ends while providing a smooth transition in the middle.

By taking the reciprocal of one plus the exponential of negative input, we get the logistic sigmoid function. No matter how large or small the input x becomes, the output is strictly trapped between zero and one. The steepness parameter k controls how sharply the transition happens around the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any real input to a smooth value between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness $k$ to see how sharply the curve transitions from flat to vertical.
reply.instructions: Change the steepness slider to see how the curve stretches or compresses. Observe how the output and slope change at the fixed marker.
